title: Petals of Blood
author: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
synopsis: Set in the rural village of Ilmorog, the novel unravels a mysterious arson attack that kills three prominent, corrupt businessmen. Through the police interrogation of four primary suspects, the narrative explores post-independence disillusionment, capitalism, and class struggle in post-colonial Kenya.

characters.name: Godfrey Munira
characters.description: The local schoolheadmaster who becomes obsessed with Wanja; driven to religious fanaticism.

characters.name: Wanja
characters.description: A resilient former barmaid and granddaughter of village elder Nyakinyua; loved by both Munira and Karega.

characters.name: Abdulla
characters.description: A disabled Mau Mau veteran and shopkeeper; acts as a protective companion to Wanja and a father figure to young Joseph.

characters.name: Karega
characters.description: A radicalized former teaching assistant and trade union organizer; ex-lover of Munira's late sister Mukami, and Wanja's true love.

title: Dust
author: Yvonne Adhiambo Owuor
synopsis: Sparked by the police shooting of Odidi Oganda in Nairobi, his sister Ajany and father Nyipir bring his body back to their remote Northern Kenya home. Odidi's murder unearths decades of suppressed national violence and family secrets dating back through Mau Mau uprisings and a shocking 1969 political assassination.

characters.name: Odidi Oganda
characters.description: A brilliant engineer turned fugitive whose death sets the story in motion; son of Nyipir and Akai.

characters.name: Ajany Oganda
characters.description: An artist living in Brazil who returns to Kenya to mourn her brother Odidi and uncover the truth behind his murder.

characters.name: Nyipir Oganda
characters.description: Ex-policeman and traumatized father; husband to Akai, bound by secrets from colonial and post-colonial conflicts.

characters.name: Akai Lokorijom
characters.description: The mercurial mother of Odidi and Ajany; harbors complex ties to a missing British colonial officer, Hugh Bolton.

characters.name: Isaiah Bolton
characters.description: An Englishman who arrives in Kenya searching for his long-lost father, Hugh Bolton, intersecting with the Oganda family.

title: Kintu
author: Jennifer Nansubuga Makumbi
synopsis: An epic spanning from 1750 to modern-day Uganda, tracing a centuries-old curse placed on Kintu Kidda—the governor of Buganda province—following the tragic death of his adopted son. The novel weaves across generations as his descendants struggle with trauma, mental illness, and identity.

characters.name: Kintu Kidda
characters.description: 18th-century Ppookino (governor); husband to twin sisters Babirye and Nnakato; accidentally triggers the ancestral curse.

characters.name: Nnakato & Babirye
characters.description: Twin wives of Kintu; Nnakato is Kintu's favorite but struggles with childlessness, while Babirye bears his children.

characters.name: Kalema
characters.description: Kintu's adopted son whose tragic death induces the ancestral curse.

characters.name: Modern Descendants (Kamu Kintu, Suubi, Miisi, Kanani)
characters.description: Descendants spread across modern Uganda who are linked by generational trauma and converge for a clan cleansing ritual.

title: Paradise
author: Abdulrazak Gurnah
synopsis: Set in pre-WWI East Africa, the story follows Yusuf, a 12-year-old boy handed over to a wealthy Arab trader to pay off his father's debts. Yusuf grows up navigating trading caravans through the African interior, witnessing colonial encroachment and forbidden love.

characters.name: Yusuf
characters.description: The observant, handsome young protagonist bonded into servitude.

characters.name: Uncle Aziz
characters.description: Wealthy Arab merchant who holds Yusuf's debt-bond; master to Yusuf and Khalil.

characters.name: Khalil
characters.description: An older servant in Aziz's store who becomes Yusuf's elder brother figure and guide.

characters.name: Zuleikha
characters.description: Aziz's sickly wife who develops an obsessive attraction toward Yusuf.

characters.name: Amina
characters.description: A young concubine held in Aziz's walled garden; Yusuf's secret love interest.

title: The Shadow King
author: Maaza Mengiste
synopsis: Set during the 1935 Italian invasion of Ethiopia, the novel highlights the critical role of women soldiers. When Emperor Haile Selassie flees into exile, a household maid named Hirut helps create a fake emperor to rally Ethiopian resistance fighters against Mussolini's army.

characters.name: Hirut
characters.description: An orphaned servant girl who becomes a fierce soldier and guardian of the "Shadow King".

characters.name: Kidane
characters.description: Ethiopian military officer and Hirut's master; husband to Aster; patriotic yet abusive toward Hirut.

characters.name: Aster
characters.description: Kidane's noble wife who rebels against traditional gender roles to organize female fighters.

characters.name: Minim (The Shadow King)
characters.description: A gentle peasant soldier resembling Haile Selassie, used by Hirut and Aster as a rallying symbol.

characters.name: Ettore Navarra
characters.description: An Italian army photographer torn between duty to fascism and his Jewish heritage.

title: Things Fall Apart
author: Chinua Achebe
synopsis: Chronicling the life of Okonkwo, a proud Igbo warrior in pre-colonial Nigeria, the story depicts traditional village life and its catastrophic disintegration following the arrival of British colonialists and Christian missionaries.

characters.name: Okonkwo
characters.description: Protagonist and wrestling champion driven by fear of appearing weak like his father, Unoka.

characters.name: Ikemefuna
characters.description: A captive boy given to the village who lives with Okonkwo's family, becoming a surrogate son to Okonkwo and brother to Nwoye.

characters.name: Nwoye
characters.description: Okonkwo's eldest son who rejects his father's harsh expectations and converts to Christianity.

characters.name: Ezinma
characters.description: Okonkwo's favorite daughter with his second wife Ekwefi; Okonkwo wishes she were a boy due to her spirit.

characters.name: Obierika
characters.description: Okonkwo's loyal best friend and voice of reason.

title: A Grain of Wheat
author: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
synopsis: Set in Kenya on the eve of Uhuru (Independence) in 1963, villagers in Thabai reflect on their actions during the Mau Mau Emergency, unearthing secrets of heroism, cowardice, and betrayal regarding the execution of resistance hero Kihika.

characters.name: Mugo
characters.description: Reclusive villager hailed as a hero for attempting to save a woman, but harboring a destructive secret about Kihika.

characters.name: Kihika
characters.description: Deceased Mau Mau guerrilla leader whose martyrdom overshadows the entire village.

characters.name: Gikonyo
characters.description: A skilled carpenter and former detainee; husband to Mumbi, struggling with her infidelity during his imprisonment.

characters.name: Mumbi
characters.description: Sister of Kihika and wife of Gikonyo; bore a child with Gikonyo's rival Karanja while Gikonyo was detained.

characters.name: Karanja
characters.description: British home guard collaborator; obsessed with Mumbi and rival to Gikonyo.

title: Unbowed
author: Wangari Maathai
synopsis: A non-fiction memoir by Nobel Peace Prize winner Wangari Maathai detailing her journey from rural Kenya to becoming an international environmental activist, politician, and founder of the Green Belt Movement.

characters.name: Wangari Maathai
characters.description: Author and activist who fought for democracy, human rights, and environmental conservation in Kenya.

characters.name: Muta Nyiro & Wanjiru
characters.description: Her supportive parents who prioritized her formal education in Nyeri.

characters.name: The Green Belt Movement Women
characters.description: The network of rural Kenyan women who partnered with Maathai to plant tens of millions of trees.

characters.name: Kenyan State Authorities
characters.description: Political opposition faced by Maathai during her peaceful demonstrations against forest land grabs.

title: The Dragonfly Sea
author: Yvonne Adhiambo Owuor
synopsis: Growing up on Pate Island off the Swahili coast, young Ayaana's world expands when genetic testing links her to Zheng He's 15th-century Chinese maritime fleet. She embarks on a journey to China and Turkey, exploring themes of identity, migration, and homecoming.

characters.name: Ayaana
characters.description: The young protagonist deeply connected to the Indian Ocean and Swahili heritage.

characters.name: Munira
characters.description: Ayaana's resilient mother who raises her on Pate Island before marrying Muhidin.

characters.name: Muhidin
characters.description: An elderly sailor who becomes Ayaana's father figure/mentor and later Munira's husband.

characters.name: Koray
characters.description: A Turkish student Ayaana meets in China; his family's shady dealings lead to her disillusionment.

characters.name: Lai Jin (Nahodha Jamal)
characters.description: A Chinese ship captain who facilitates Ayaana's travel to China.

title: The River Between
author: Ngũgĩ wa Thiong'o
synopsis: Set in two opposing Gikuyu ridges (Makuyu and Kameno) separated by the Honia River, the novel details the cultural rift caused by Christian missionaries and traditional preservation, centered around a young leader trying to unify his people.

characters.name: Waiyaki
characters.description: Young idealist leader from Kameno who seeks to unite both ridges through Western education while honoring Gikuyu traditions.

characters.name: Nyambura
characters.description: Daughter of the fanatical Christian convert Joshua; falls in love with Waiyaki across religious divides.

characters.name: Muthoni
characters.description: Nyambura's younger sister who seeks both Christian faith and traditional Gikuyu circumcision, resulting in her tragic death.

characters.name: Chege
characters.description: Waiyaki's father, a traditional seer who passes ancient prophecies down to his son.

characters.name: Kabonyi
characters.description: Rival elder who leads the traditionalist council and seeks to destroy Waiyaki.
